title: Is this the "one giant hole", or a sprawl of 2-cell scratches?
question: You said they dig one giant hole right now. The new chamber census disagrees and I want your eye on which reading is right, because the two need opposite fixes. It says nothing anywhere in this nest is more than 2 cells across -- no 8-cell square fits anywhere in it, at ants=40, 150, 300 or 600. So it reads as a scratch network sprawled across 150 columns rather than a cavern. Looking at it: is the problem that it is too WIDE and merged (stop it merging), or that it is too THIN everywhere (make it dig wider)?
context_md:
Your spec, 2026-09-20: passage ~4 cells across, chambers 8-16 tall, wider than tall, 2-4x contrast.

New `digbox` column scores exactly that -- a distance transform over the room, so a chamber is somewhere an 8-cell square fits. Proven on three carved beds: a target nest reads 2 chambers / 12h x 32w / contrast 3.0x, one 120x14 hole reads 1 chamber 120 wide, and 2-cell galleries read 0 chambers.

Pointed at the real colony it reads **0 chambers, passage bore 2** at every colony size.

Same column on the founding shaft from PR #482: its entrance chamber is carved two rows tall (`for dy in 0..2`) and up to 25 long -- the exact shape you just ruled unreadable. Shaft is 2 wide against your 4.

7 stops top to bottom, 12,000 frames, 300 ants, no food in the box.
